record.paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
record.original_question: Is every retract of a co-sober T0 space again co-sober?

evidence.quote: Question 9.6. Is a retract of a co-sober space co-sober?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $X$ be a topological space. A nonempty closed subset $A\subseteq X$ is called irreducible if whenever $A=B\cup C$ with $B,C$ closed, then $A=B$ or $A=C$. The space $X$ is sober if it is $T_0$ and every irreducible closed subset is the closure $\overline{\{x\}}$ of a unique point $x\in X$.

A subset $K\subseteq X$ is saturated if $K$ equals the intersection of all open sets containing it (equivalently, $K$ is an upper set in the specialization order $\leq$ defined by $x\leq y\iff x\in\overline{\{y\}}$). A nonempty compact saturated subset $K\subseteq X$ is called $k$-irreducible (or supercompact / irreducible compact saturated) if whenever $K\subseteq U\cup V$ with $U,V$ open, then $K\subseteq U$ or $K\subseteq V$. The space $X$ is called co-sober if it is $T_0$ and every $k$-irreducible compact saturated subset of $X$ is of the form ${\uparrow}x=\{y\in X: x\leq y\}$ for some (necessarily unique) $x\in X$.

A subspace $Y\subseteq X$ is called a retract of $X$ if there exists a continuous map $r:X\to Y$, called a retraction, such that $r(y)=y$ for every $y\in Y$ (equivalently, $r\circ i=\mathrm{id}_Y$ where $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ is the inclusion).

Problem. Suppose $X$ is a co-sober $T_0$ topological space and $Y\subseteq X$ is a retract of $X$ (in particular, $Y$ is then a $T_0$ space in the subspace topology). Must $Y$ also be co-sober?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not reveal a published resolution to the question of whether retracts of co-sober $T_0$ spaces are co-sober. Related results in the literature (e.g., closed and saturated subspaces of co-sober spaces are co-sober; not every sober space is co-sober) are known, but the specific retract problem appears to remain unresolved as of the searches performed.

status_evidence.title: Sober is not always co-sober - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexample showing sober spaces need not be co-sober; discusses properties of co-sober spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Co-sober spaces are an active topic; related sub-space results exist but retract case not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Sober Scott Spaces are not always co-sober
status_evidence.snippet: Further work on co-sobriety in domain theory.
status_evidence.claim: Recent research continues on co-sober properties without resolving the retract question.
